rationale: Tiger closed an infrastructure-strategy investment in American Natural parent Cleopatra Resources on May 28, 2015, but the reviewed primary sources do not support the repository's Fund I attribution, sole-owner presentation or an ownership percentage. Cleopatra sold substantially all American Natural convenience-retail assets to Giant Oil in December 2023. The retained manager-level perimeter is American Natural Supply, an asset-based commercial fuel-supply, storage, terminal and logistics network. Tiger's current board representation and live portfolio listing support continuing involvement, while no full Tiger exit or sale of retained ANS was found.
recommendedChanges: Retain one active United States canonical company at american-natural|united-states, but define the current perimeter as Cleopatra Resources' retained American Natural Supply business.
Preserve Tiger's May 28, 2015 entry while setting fund, vehicle, security and stake to NOT_PUBLICLY_DISCLOSED; do not infer Fund I or sole ownership.
Record the December 2023 sale of substantially all American Natural Retail PA assets to Giant Oil as a partial platform divestiture.
Exclude Giant-owned retail stores and keep individual stations beneath their operator rather than creating separate PortCos.
Classify the retained business from current evidence as commercial fuel-supply, storage, terminal and logistics infrastructure rather than a predominantly alternative-fuel retail platform.
unresolvedQuestions: Tiger's exact current stake, fund, vehicle, security, co-investors and the identity or control effect of the 2022 equity investor are not publicly disclosed.
Orion/OIC's current security and governance rights are not publicly disclosed.
Current ANS terminal count, fleet, contracts, throughput and CNG/RNG/EV share are not publicly disclosed.
